Compared with the state-of-the-art multitask models, the hdADMET model achieved competitive performance with a significantly lower computational cost. Its practical utility was further demonstrated by accurately predicting the ADMET profiles of newly identified NPs mined from the literature studies. The promising candidate with high anticancer activity, low toxicity, and favorable metabolic properties was identified for further experimental validation. The hdADMET model offered an alternative way to prioritize leading compounds for clinical translation through HN embeddings and deep learning.

desc: [International emergency nursing] Polytrauma triage requires rapid prioritization under conditions of incomplete information, physiological instability, crowding, and high consequences of error. Machine learning (ML) is increasingly discussed as a means of strengthening emergency triage; however, the concept of ML-supported polytrauma triage decision support remains insufficiently defined for emergency nursing, particularly regarding its temporal and clinical boundaries within the emergency department. This concept analysis clarifies the meaning, defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, empirical referents, and boundaries of machine learning-supported polytrauma triage decision support. Walker and Avant's concept analysis method guided the analysis. A structured and traceable literature identification process was used to examine literature on polytrauma, initial emergency department triage, clinical decision support, machine learning in emergency and trauma care, digital nursing decision-making, and artificial intelligence safety. Sources were mapped using a concept-analysis matrix to identify concept uses, candidate attributes, antecedents, consequences, cases, empirical referents, and conceptual boundaries. Machine learning-supported polytrauma triage decision support was defined as a human-in-the-loop clinical decision support process operating within the initial emergency department triage window, in which ML integrates polytrauma-relevant information available at or immediately before the first triage decision and generates time-critical acuity or near-term deterioration estimates to inform immediate prioritization without replacing clinician judgment. Three core defining attributes were identified: polytrauma-relevant initial-triage data integration, time-critical triage risk or acuity estimation, and human-in-the-loop clinical decision support. Model validation, workflow fit and interpretability, and performance governance were distinguished from defining attributes and positioned as antecedent or implementation conditions and empirical referents for safe clinical use. The concept is distinct from conventional triage, trauma scoring, post-triage prognostic modeling, generic clinical decision support, and automated decision-making. Clarifying both its defining attributes and its temporal boundary positions ML as a support for the initial emergency nursing triage decision rather than as a substitute for professional judgment or a broader trauma management system.

source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Protein thermodynamic stability changes upon mutation profoundly affect protein structure and biological function. Recent advances in deep learning and protein language models have provided powerful tools for computational analysis of mutation-induced stability changes. However, most existing methods focus on quantitative regression of free-energy changes, which places strong dependence on precise experimentally measured ΔΔG values, although reliably determining the direction of stability change is itself an important objective in many practical applications. Here, we propose BlindDDG, a novel framework that reformulates protein mutation stability prediction from quantitative ΔΔG estimation to direction-oriented stability change classification. First, we introduce a blind-evaluation strategy that models mutation-induced changes by learning the representation difference between wild-type and mutant proteins, rather than relying solely on their individual intrinsic properties. This formulation focuses on the direction of stability changes and reduces the dependence on precise quantitative ΔΔG measurements. Second, a Siamese architecture with shared parameters is employed to encode the wild-type and mutant states and capture subtle mutation-associated differences. Third, a local structure-aware cross-attention mechanism is developed to integrate mutation-centered structural information with global protein language model representations, enabling effective multimodal feature interaction. Experimental results on the independent S669 benchmark demonstrate that BlindDDG achieves strong classification performance, obtaining an F1 score of 0.5449, an MCC of 0.3929, an accuracy of 0.7721, and a recall of 0.5417 for stabilizing mutation identification. BlindDDG outperforms all evaluated methods in F1 score, MCC, accuracy, and recall, highlighting its effectiveness in capturing mutation-induced stability changes, particularly for imbalanced stability classification.

desc: [RSC advances] The traditional analytical methods for detecting environmentally or biologically important analytes are sensitive, but not suitable for rapid on-site analysis because they require complex instrumentation and laboratory facilities. Optical Schiff base-based chemosensors and biosensors are promising tools owing to their tunable photophysical properties, and colorimetry or fluorescence sensing modes. Recent literature on Schiff base-based optical chemosensors developed for the detection of environmental and biologically important analytes such as metal ions, toxic anions, environmental pollutants and clinically important biomolecules published from January 2020 to 31 July 2026 is critically reviewed. This review discusses structure-property relationships and sensing performance. In addition, important photophysical processes like intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), chelation-enhanced or chelation-quenched fluorescence (CHEF/CHEQ), excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), aggregation-induced emission (AIE), and analytical performance parameters, including sensitivity, selectivity, detection limits, linear ranges, response times, and applicability to real samples, were evaluated. Also, special attention was given to new approaches that combine molecular design with computational tools, chemometric data analysis, microfluidic devices and portable digital tools to enhance analytical performance and to increase applicability in real-world applications. source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Vast knowledge dispersed across the unstructured literature remains an indispensable complement to photoresist development. However, the intricate relationships among formulation, processing, and performance are not only scattered throughout publications but also complicated by semantic heterogeneity and contextual ambiguity, hindering knowledge management that extends beyond simple retrieval. To address these issues, we employed large language models (LLMs) to construct a photoresist material knowledge graph (KG) covering synthesis, properties, and applications. From nearly 12,000 full-text documents, we extracted 320,000 entities, 178,000 relationships, and 1,172,000 attribute entries. desc: [International orthodontics] To present a fully automated artificial intelligence (AI) workflow to generate personalized orthodontic target set-ups and compare the quality of the occlusal outcome with manual set-ups, using the American Board of Orthodontics Model Grading System (ABO MGS). The AI workflow takes an intraoral scan and performs tooth segmentation, landmark detection, tooth completion, and tooth alignment to generate a 3D-printable personalized set-up without human intervention. The occlusal outcome was evaluated on twenty non-extraction full jaw cases treated with customized fixed appliances by comparing the AI set-ups to manual set-ups made by experienced laboratory technicians. Both set-up series were scored with the ABO MGS for alignment and rotations, marginal ridges, buccolingual inclination, overjet, occlusal contacts, occlusal relationships, and interproximal contacts. The 'alignment and rotations' category was additionally analysed separately for the anterior (canine to canine) and posterior (premolars to second molars) segments. Paired comparisons used the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test (α=0.05). Based on the total ABO MGS scores, the AI set-ups (mean: 14.95) and manual set-ups (mean: 12.20) showed high-quality occlusal outcomes, which were both far below the ABO passing score. AI set-ups showed significantly more penalty points for alignment and rotations (median: 8 vs. 5; P<0.001). This difference was confined to the posterior segments; anterior alignment was near-ideal for both methods. Other categories did not differ significantly (P=0.082-0.886). For the first time, a fully automated AI-based 3D workflow generated personalized orthodontic target set-ups for non-extraction cases with a clinically acceptable, high-quality occlusal outcome, in approximately four minutes. Posterior alignment remains the only shortcoming of the AI set-ups and is the obvious target for further algorithm refinement or brief manual correction.

title: Coordinated online manipulation in the era of generative AI: emerging challenges.
desc: [Frontiers in sociology] Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly transforming the communicative processes through which coordinated online manipulation is produced, personalized, and coordinated at unprecedented scale, raising growing concerns about its societal implications. This Mini Review critically examines empirical research published during the first 3 years of widespread public accessibility of GenAI to assess how these developments are reshaping Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior (CIB) across different societal domains. Three interconnected developments consistently emerge: the transformation of communicative production through scalable, personalized, and multimodal content generation; increasing AI-assisted coordination of influence campaigns; and new forms of communicative vulnerability associated with increasingly human-like synthetic communication. Together, these developments suggest that coordinated influence is becoming more adaptive, persistent, and difficult to recognize within evolving human-AI communicative configurations. Beyond synthesizing recent empirical evidence, the review identifies emerging conceptual and methodological challenges concerning communicative agency, coordination, and authenticity, while outlining future directions for sociological research. Overall, the growing use of GenAI in evolving CIB poses significant risks to public trust, opinion formation, and democratic discourse, underscoring the urgency of understanding and addressing this rapidly evolving phenomenon.

title: Thermodynamically Guided CRISPR Spacer Optimization: Strategy-Dependent Off-Target Trade-Offs.
source: PubMed · Journal of chemical information and modeling
desc: [Journal of chemical information and modeling] Most CRISPR-Cas9 design tools select guide RNAs (gRNAs) by ranking predefined candidates rather than actively optimizing them. Here we instead formulate SpCas9 spacer refinement as a constrained search problem, in which a limited number of nucleotide substitutions may be introduced outside the PAM-proximal seed region. The search is driven by a thermodynamically grounded objective that combines CRISPRspec-based specificity with penalties for suboptimal GC content and long homopolymer runs. Within this single setting we compare five search strategies: three reinforcement-learning (RL) policies, which are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Quantile-Regression Deep Q-Network (QR-DQN), and Rainbow Deep Q-Network (Rainbow DQN), together with a nonlearning score-guided search and a prompt-guided large language model (LLM). All five share the same objective, mutable positions, substitution budget, and evaluation protocol, so that only the search strategy differs. On 100 held-out IGF2R guides from a gene and chromosome excluded from training, every strategy significantly reduced the predicted off-target burden (38.6-78.3%) and improved independent specificity metrics without degrading on-target scores. title: Medical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Development and Evaluation of the MedEvalArena Benchmark.

title: GPT-4-Assisted Versus Human Detection of Intraoperative Adverse Events From Spine Surgery Operative Reports.
desc: [Neurosurgery practice] Manual chart review remains the primary method of clinical data collection in spine surgery research but is time intensive and prone to human error. Large language models may enable automated extraction of clinically meaningful events from unstructured operative text. We evaluated the performance of generative pre-trained transformer 4 (GPT-4) in detecting intraoperative adverse events from spine surgery operative notes compared with trained human reviewers. A retrospective cohort of 1454 laminectomy cases performed at a single academic institution between 2016 and 2022 was analyzed. Deidentified operative notes were independently reviewed by 4 trained human reviewers and GPT-4 using standardized prompts to identify incidental durotomy and nondurotomy intraoperative adverse events. Discordant classifications were adjudicated by a senior reviewer to establish ground truth. Performance metrics including sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and F1 score were calculated. Analyses were stratified by operative note length, and review time was estimated. Incidental durotomy occurred in 88 cases (6.1%). GPT-4 achieved 100.0% sensitivity compared with 89.8% for human reviewers, with lower positive predictive value (88.0% vs 100.0%) but similar specificity (99.1% vs 100.0%). For nondurotomy adverse events (n = 21), GPT-4 demonstrated higher sensitivity than humans (90.5% vs 57.1%) with equivalent specificity (100.0%). GPT-4 maintained stable performance across note length quartiles, whereas human reviewer sensitivity decreased for longer notes. Human reviewers required approximately 35 hours to review all notes, compared with approximately 2 hours for GPT-4. GPT-4 demonstrated higher observed sensitivity than trained human reviewers for detecting intraoperative adverse events from spine surgery operative reports while reducing review time by more than 90%. Large language model-assisted chart review may serve as a scalable human-in-the-loop adjunct to traditional chart review, improving the completeness and efficiency of neurosurgical outcomes research.

title: Automated Approaches to Extracting Arm-Level Numerical Results From Published Studies for Meta-Analysis.
desc: [Campbell systematic reviews] Systematic reviews depend on accurate extraction of outcome data from primary studies, yet this step remains largely manual and time-consuming. Automation tools exist for identifying and retrieving studies and for extracting non-numeric study characteristics, but few target the numerical arm-level results needed for meta-analysis. We developed and evaluated a hybrid approach for extracting arm-level results (number of events and number enrolled per arm) for binary outcomes from two-arm randomized controlled trials published as PDFs. Rule-based string processing in R locates and parses results tables and candidate sentences in the Results section; a large language model (ChatGPT, accessed through the OpenAI API) is then used only to structure the numerical information in the selected sentences. We evaluated the approach by replicating a Cochrane meta-analysis of favipiravir for COVID-19 (11 trials; all-cause mortality at 28 to 30 days). Table-based extraction was applied to five articles and in-line text extraction to six. The extracted data matched the published arm-level results for all studies except one, where the pipeline recovered a sample size (24) consistent with the trial's results table rather than its text (25). The replicated random-effects meta-analysis gave a summary risk ratio of 0.84 (95% CI 0.49-1.46), identical to the original review, with minor differences in study weights attributable to rounding. An independent test on infectious bovine keratoconjunctivitis vaccine trials showed partial transferability, with failures confined to scanned PDFs and complex table structures. The code and the list of extracted articles are publicly available on GitHub.

title: Reimagining inflammatory bowel disease in the age of artificial intelligence: discovery, care, education, and sustainability for the next decade.
desc: [Journal of Crohn's & colitis] Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly evolving from task-specific algorithms to multimodal foundation models capable of integrating heterogeneous biological and clinical data across the health-care continuum. In inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), this transformation offers an unprecedented opportunity to move beyond fragmented analyses toward a unified understanding and management of disease. Artificial intelligence is emerging as the connective infrastructure linking scientific discovery, therapeutic development, patient care, education, and health-care delivery systems into continuously learning ecosystems. In this viewpoint, we explore how AI may reshape IBD over the next decade through 5 interconnected domains. Advances in multimodal AI accelerate biological discovery by integrating multiomics, spatial biology, and foundation models to identify mechanistic disease endotypes. Simultaneously, AI can shorten the path from molecular discovery to therapeutic innovation by supporting target identification, predicting protein structure, drug positioning, and adaptive clinical trial design. These scientific advances converge at the bedside, where multimodal AI may transform patient care from reactive management to predictive precision medicine through integrated diagnostics, digital biomarkers, real-time monitoring and individualized risk prediction. Beyond clinical care, AI is redefining medical education by enabling adaptive learning, explainable decision support, and democratized specialist expertise, while contributing to sustainable health care through optimized resource allocation, workforce support, and continuously learning systems. Realizing this vision will require robust governance, interoperability, prospective validation, and equitable implementation. If responsibly deployed, AI holds the potential to redefine IBD diagnosis, classification, therapeutic strategies and management within an intelligent ecosystem able to accelerate discovery, personalize care, and improve outcomes for patients and health-care systems alike.

title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
desc: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0, RoboSPA, and RMBench demonstrate the effectiveness of Embodied-Harness in generalization under environmental variations, spatial reasoning, long-horizon planning, and memory-dependent manipulation. Our method achieves success rates of 82.4%, 76.7%, and 94.4% on the three benchmarks, respectively. Real-world evaluation further yields an average success rate of 96.7% across three manipulation tasks. These results highlight the potential of Embodied-Harness to improve robotic manipulation through experience-driven harness self-improvement.

title: Medical Specialty Prediction from Bangla Patient Narratives: A Comparative Study of ML, DL, Transformers, and LLMs
desc: Timely access to appropriate medical specialists remains a bottleneck in Bangladesh's healthcare system, as patients describe symptoms in informal Bangla rather than clinical terms, leading to ineffective referrals. This paper compares four model families for predicting medical specialties from Bangla patient narratives: six machine learning (ML) models using hybrid TF-IDF features, four deep learning (DL) models using Word2Vec embeddings trained on the corpus, four fine-tuned transformers, and five large language models (LLMs) evaluated zero-shot. From a corpus of 3798 patient records covering 20 specialties, we retained the five with the most records (Medicine, Gynecology, Dermatology, Pediatrics, Gastroenterology) and split the resulting 2730 records 80:20 into training and test sets shared by all families. The best transformer was XLM-RoBERTa (86.26% accuracy, 86.21% macro-F1), the best ML model was SVM (84.98%, 84.92%), the best DL model was Bidirectional GRU (80.77%, 80.83%), and the best LLM was Gemini (90.29%, 90.15%). Holm-corrected paired McNemar tests show SVM significantly outperforming Bi-LSTM (adjusted p = 0.004), whereas the Gemini-versus-Grok gap does not survive correction (adjusted p = 0.104), and neither the strongest transformer versus the weakest LLM (Grok) nor SVM versus the strongest transformer reaches significance. A tuned classical model is thus statistically indistinguishable from the strongest transformer, so accuracy rankings alone should not be read as evidence of one family's superiority. The findings provide a comparative baseline for Bangla medical text classification.

title: rendehR: a cohort-first, provenance-aware, agentic-ready pipeline for harmonizing multi-source electronic health records
desc: Objective: Public electronic health record (EHR) databases differ in schema, identifiers, coding systems, units, and event structure, making disease-specific studies across multiple sources difficult to construct and audit. We developed rendehR, a computational pipeline and R package for cohort-centered extraction and harmonization of multi-source EHR data. Materials and Methods: rendehR treats cohort definition as an explicit executable component of dataset construction. Cohorts can be defined using diagnosis codes, identifiers, R callbacks, or source-specific SQL. After cohort selection, linked source tables are restricted to the selected population and can be retained as cohort-specific Parquet datasets or loaded into a persistent database. Clinical concepts are defined using source-aware mappings, generated, or curated SQL and are harmonized into flat, time-series, and duration representations. Configuration, executable SQL, cohort metadata, concept-origin metadata, and source-level values are retained to support inspection and traceability. In the current version rendehR provides interactive R assistant wizards for workflow configuration, a Shiny application for patient-level data visualization, three agent skills for AI-assisted workflow execution and extension, and an MCP server exposing nine read-only tools for AI-assisted configuration, concept discovery, and cohort exploration. The current implementation supports MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU-CRD. We demonstrate rendehR on a reference cohort of spinal cord injury and disease (SCID). Results: Using the reference cohort, rendehR identified 4,320, 39,850, and 2,343 qualifying hospital admissions in MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, and eICU-CRD, respectively. Patient-level extraction expanded these cohorts to 5,725, 104,988, and 2,823 hospital admissions, with 5,983, 17,405, and 3,441 associated ICU stays, respectively. Applying the more complex Sepsis-3 case identification, rendehR identified and extracted 34,460, 41,296, and 47,035 qualifying ICU stays across the same databases, respectively. The current concept library includes 22 flat, 123 time-series, and 75 duration harmonized concepts. Conclusion: rendehR provides a cohort-centered framework for constructing disease-specific datasets from multiple heterogeneous HER sources while preserving the source-specific logic used to define cohorts and clinical concepts. title: Precision diabetes care through advanced clinical assessment biomarkers artificial intelligence and personalized therapeutics.
source: PubMed · Therapeutic advances in endocrinology and metabolism
desc: [Therapeutic advances in endocrinology and metabolism] There is a great heterogeneity in disease characteristics, progression, manifestations, and treatment efficacy that make population-level strategies based on diabetes mellitus ineffective. Precision medicine provides ways to tackle this disparity by combining clinical, genetic, molecular, metabolic and behavioural data with the goal of personalized diagnosis, risk stratification or choosing treatment. This review covers a comprehensive and clinically relevant assessment of personalized diabetes care and the emerging research areas of the associated biomarkers, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics, pharmacogenomics, nutrigenomics, continuous glucose monitoring, wearable technologies, digital health and artificial intelligence-based decision support systems. Molecular characterization, patient stratification, personalised pharmacotherapy, lifestyle intervention, and long-term digital monitoring is integrated with these technologies rather than being considered separate entities. The main focus is on the clinical and/or translational implications of these strategies, such as their current evidence strength and their limitations, population diversity, external validation, cost-effectiveness, data interoperability, privacy and healthcare implementation. Combining the multi-omics and real-time digital information with traditional clinical evaluation could make it possible to better manage diabetes in a more predictive, adaptive, patient-centred manner. Yet, future validation, standardized analysis tools, access, and tools to be designed into standard clinical practice are still vital to bringing precision diabetes strategies from novel technologies into practical care.

title: Synthetic EHR Generators Should Be Audited Like LLMs
desc: Synthetic electronic health record (EHR) generation is increasingly adopting large autoregressive models, yet privacy evaluation has not kept pace, relying heavily on similarity-based heuristics and aggregate metrics that can obscure patient-specific memorisation. We argue that these models should additionally undergo LLM-style memorisation audits at the level of individual patient records. We support this position by comparing membership-inference evaluations across four prominent autoregressive EHR generators, highlighting inconsistent evaluation practices in patient representations and attack procedures. We evaluate trajectory reconstruction from partial context and introduce randomly assigned patient-level canaries to distinguish memorised associations from clinical generalisation. We examine these methods in a GPT-2-style model deliberately overfit to 1,000 MIMIC-IV patient trajectories, creating a controlled setting in which memorisation should be readily detectable. The model systematically recovers training patients' canaries, and their trajectory reconstruction approaches perfect accuracy with increasing context. Held-out patients show no systematic canary recovery, while reconstruction remains low and improves only marginally with additional context. These experiments establish a positive-control baseline for further evaluation of these methods in realistically trained models.

title: Continually pretrained open-weight language models can outperform traditional machine learning in EHR-based clinical prediction
desc: Large language models (LLMs) prompted with electronic health record (EHR) data have predicted clinical outcomes less accurately than locally trained machine-learning models. We developed VEX-EHR by extending the vocabulary of a 12-billion-parameter open-weight LLM (weights publicly available) with 17,601 clinical and audit-log codes from 170,483 patients' records at one academic medical center, continuing its pretraining on those 2019-2024 records (4.7 billion tokens) and fine-tuning it per task. AUROCs were 0.917 for next-24-hour discharge, 0.715 for 30-day readmission and 0.847 for intensive care unit acute kidney injury, against 0.868, 0.677 and 0.828 for gradient-boosted trees and 0.848, 0.650 and 0.791 for CEHR-BERT, an EHR foundation model. Continued pretraining added 0.031-0.053 AUROC on every task. With 10% of the labels, VEX-EHR exceeded both comparators using all labels for discharge, and CEHR-BERT for readmission, valuable where labels are costly. Adapted by continued pretraining, open-weight LLMs can outperform traditional machine learning in EHR-based prediction.

A Multiagent Large Language Model Framework for Longitudinal Multimodal Tracking of Wet Age-Related Macular Degeneration: Retrospective Feasibility Study.
desc: [JMIR formative research] Wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD) requires long-term, high-frequency management involving multimodal retinal imaging across repeated follow-up visits. Reconstructing disease trajectories from fragmented imaging reports, treatment histories, and clinical notes creates a substantial information integration burden for clinicians in routine chronic disease management. This study aimed to evaluate the preliminary feasibility of a proof-of-concept, multiagent large language model (LLM) framework that integrates longitudinal multimodal imaging findings and treatment records into structured reports to support clinician review during wet AMD follow-up. We developed a 3-layer multiagent LLM framework using GPT-4o and AutoGen. The framework consisted of modality-specific perception agents using a visual grounding prompting strategy, an integration agent, and a tracking report agent. To test technical feasibility, the framework was evaluated on a dense retrospective pilot dataset of 12 patients encompassing 69 long-term follow-up visits. AI-generated outputs were assessed against expert review at the visit level and through report-level quality scoring. In this exploratory cohort, the framework achieved a mean visit-level activity classification accuracy of 80.8% (SD 3.4%) across 4 independent runs (range 78.3%-85.5%), with a mean Cohen κ of 0.605 (SD 0.072; range 0.549-0.705). The framework generated structured longitudinal summaries of disease activity, multimodal findings, and treatment histories. The visual grounding prompting strategy reduced the nonimage reference rate from 13.8% (12/87) to 1.1% (1/87), supporting more consistent grounding of image-based outputs in visual evidence. This proof-of-concept study supports the preliminary feasibility of using a multiagent LLM framework to organize longitudinal multimodal wet AMD follow-up data and produce structured summaries for clinician review. These reports are intended to support review of disease progression and treatment response associations during longitudinal follow-up. Future prospective multicenter studies with larger patient cohorts should evaluate whether these reports improve clinical workflow efficiency, reduce clinician workload, and support follow-up management decisions.

title: Laya-IsoToken: Day-One Clinical Codebook Switching via Closed-Form Operator Compilation
desc: Healthcare systems periodically revise diagnostic and procedural classifications (ICD-9 to ICD-10/11), update hospital reimbursement groupers (MS-DRG), and deploy clinical coding across languages. Supervised coding networks bind clinical text encoders to fixed per-code classifier weights, forcing hospitals to re-annotate tens of thousands of records before switching codebooks, whereas standalone large language models incur high latency and hallucinate invalid codes. Here we show that day-one clinical codebook switching becomes feasible without target-labeled notes when local clinical evidence reading is decoupled from a strictly frozen multilingual concept space. Laya-IsoToken trains a clinical span reader once on source records with zero per-code classifier parameters, separating text evidence from historical disease prevalence. Given only public target code descriptions, closed-form matrix compilation aligns distributional shifts, compensates for paraphrased definitions, and deduplicates sibling codes in under three seconds, while a pre-deployment geometric residual routes unfamiliar concepts to offline language model verification. Across 32,804 MIMIC-IV ICD-9 discharges, Laya-IsoToken matches published supervised baselines (62.6% Micro-F1) while reducing active calibration error by 32%. Switched with zero target training notes to 13,783 unseen-patient ICD-10 discharges, MS-DRG groups, and multilingual cohorts, it outperforms biomedical dense retrievers, semantic crosswalks (+5.4 F1 points on ICD-10, paired $d_z = 0.49$, $p < 0.001$), and official US CMS equivalence mappings (+3.5 points, $p < 0.001$) at 9.4 ms per admission. Pairing this reader with an offline 31B verifier across 1,000 full discharge summaries lifts zero-training ICD-10 coding to 40.6% Micro-F1 (57.0% category F1, $d_z = 0.66$, $p < 0.001$) with 0.0% invalid code hallucinations.

title: STREAM: Sequential Transformer for Risk Estimation from Asynchronous Medical Events for Dynamic Postoperative AKI Prediction
desc: Postoperative acute kidney injury (PO-AKI) risk estimates evolve as clinical information accumulates, yet many electronic health record (EHR) models use static or fixed-window representations. We developed STREAM, a perioperative event-stream Transformer that represents irregular EHR data as chronological clinical events and supports surgery-index prediction at surgery completion and event-by-event postoperative AKI prediction. In a retrospective cohort of 167,078 noncardiac surgical episodes, STREAM achieved surgery-index AUROC/AUPRC of 0.942/0.771, the Time-series Transformer 0.933/0.729, and GRU-D 0.926/0.695. Postoperative macro-AUPRC across 6-hour evaluation intervals was 0.589, 0.525, and 0.547, respectively. STREAM showed more consistent calibration across postoperative time points than the comparators. Event-arrival attribution and within-window permutation analysis enabled event-level interpretation of how newly arrived information and fine-grained event ordering shaped evolving risk estimates. These findings support event-stream modeling as an interpretable framework for dynamic, temporally resolved prediction from longitudinal EHR data as well as a potential risk-estimation component for future perioperative digital twins.

From detection to clinical comprehension: a cognitive hierarchy for the epistemic and ethical limits of artificial intelligence in radiology.
desc: [La Radiologia medica] Artificial intelligence (AI) detects findings in medical images at a level that, for specific tasks, matches or exceeds that of an expert radiologist. Detecting a finding, however, is not the same as understanding a disease. AI radiology literature rarely distinguishes between these two processes. This article proposes a four-level cognitive hierarchy, inspired by Ackoff's [1] model of data, information, knowledge, and wisdom, to analyze at which level current AI operates and its epistemic and ethical consequences. The four levels, detection, classification, diagnosis, and clinical comprehension, form a gradient of increasing cognitive demand. The last of these corresponds to the tacit knowledge described by Polanyi [2] and is consistent with classic studies of radiological perception. Recent literature on epistemic authority in medicine suggests that the gap between this level and AI reflects, at least in part, a difference in the type of justification underpinning clinical judgment. AI reliably automates the first two levels, makes partial progress on the third when structured clinical data are available, and currently lacks an operational counterpart for the fourth. This distinction has implications for the training of specialists and for clinical responsibility, which remains with the radiologist in AI-assisted diagnosis.

title: When Should We Trust Medical Image Models? Evaluating Confidence Reliability under Cross-Dataset Shift
desc: Deep learning models for chest X-ray analysis often achieve strong performance on benchmark datasets, but their reliability under cross-dataset deployment remains unclear. In clinical practice, models trained in one hospital system may be applied to data from another, where distributional and labeling differences can affect both prediction accuracy and model confidence. We conduct a controlled empirical study of model confidence under cross-dataset transfer. We train ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 on CheXpert and evaluate them on MIMIC-CXR across five experimental settings, focusing on Pneumothorax and Pleural Effusion. We measure predictive performance using AUC and confidence reliability using Expected Calibration Error (ECE), Brier score, and average confidence on incorrect predictions, all reported with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. We further evaluate post-hoc temperature scaling fit on the source validation set and use Grad-CAM to examine the mechanism behind cross-domain performance differences. Cross-domain AUC drops 7-13 percentage points, and the best in-domain model is not the best cross-domain model. Source-domain temperature scaling produces marginal ECE changes but systematically increases confidence on incorrect predictions across all four model-pathology combinations. Grad-CAM reveals that DenseNet relies on a concentrated spatial prior that fails to transfer, while ResNet's more distributed attention generalizes better. These findings argue for cross-site validation and safety-specific calibration metrics in medical AI evaluation.

title: Co-occurrence Is Not Evidence: Separating Protein-Disease Findings from Incidental Mentions in HFpEF Literature
desc: Literature-mining pipelines such as CaseOLAP rank proteins by how often they appear next to a disease term. Appearing next to a disease is not the same as being implicated in it: in our 300-sentence held-out set of PubMed sentences that mention a protein and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), only 115 assert a biological association. The rest report a negative finding or mention the protein in passing, for example as a drug the patients were taking. We train a sentence-level filter that sorts each protein mention into associated, not_associated or incidental. It is a fine-tuned PubMedBERT trained with class-weighted cross-entropy and R-Drop regularization, combined into a six-model majority-vote ensemble over three random seeds. On the held-out set, with no thresholds tuned on it, the ensemble reaches 85.3% accuracy and 86.1% macro F1 (bootstrap 95% confidence intervals 81.0-89.3% and 82.1-89.7%), against 38.3% accuracy for the co-occurrence baseline, which counts every mention as an association. Single models average 84.4 +/- 0.7% accuracy across seeds. Run after CaseOLAP, the filter removes protein mentions that are not evidence of association from the HFpEF candidate list. Where the ensemble's majority vote disagreed with the annotation, the annotation was often wrong. Expert review of those sentences corrected 53 of 88 flagged evaluation labels and 109 training labels. Most of the errors came from one flaw in the annotation sheet: in sentences naming several proteins, it did not say which protein the label was for. The audit stage coincided with the largest accuracy gain in the project, but the same stage also changed the evaluation labels and the training loss, so we report it as a chronology, not as a controlled result.

title: Next-generation multispecific antibodies for oncology: mechanisms and clinical translation.
source: PubMed · Signal transduction and targeted therapy
desc: [Signal transduction and targeted therapy] Monoclonal antibodies are central to modern targeted cancer therapy and immunotherapy. However, clonal heterogeneity and dynamic changes in the tumor microenvironment can enable solid tumors to evade single-target therapies. Multispecific antibodies offer a strategy to address these limitations by integrating distinct binding specificities within a single molecule. Yet neither increasing the number of targets nor increasing binding affinity alone guarantees clinical benefit. A central challenge is to coordinate immune-cell redirection, conditional activation, and Boolean logic gating with precise spatial and temporal control. These capabilities must be achieved while ensuring molecular developability, meeting chemistry, manufacturing, and controls requirements, and maintaining an adequate therapeutic window. Using intended biological function as the organizing principle, this Review examines how molecular architecture, affinity engineering, Fc-region engineering, and logic-gated design shape pharmacological profiles and clinical safety. We also discuss the implications of internalization kinetics for bispecific antibody-drug conjugates. We then examine mechanisms of therapeutic resistance and immune-niche remodeling within the tumor microenvironment and assess progress in clinical translation. Particular attention is given to the fidelity of preclinical models, biomarker limitations, strategies to widen the therapeutic window, and combination and sequential treatment regimens. Finally, we discuss emerging directions, including logic-gated activation, in situ immune priming with oncolytic viruses or vaccines, and artificial intelligence-guided antibody design. Together, these perspectives provide a framework for aligning molecular design with biological context and translational requirements to guide the development of next-generation multispecific cancer therapeutics.

title: GAG-Net: Graph-Based Anatomical Guidance Network for Pharyngeal Area Segmentation in VFSS Images
desc: Diagnosing sarcopenic dysphagia typically requires costly supplementary imaging such as CT or MRI to assess muscle atrophy, burdening elderly patients. The pharyngeal area at rest (PA_rest), measurable directly from videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS) images, is a promising biomarker that could eliminate this dependency, but repeated manual measurement has limited its adoption. PA_rest segmentation is further complicated by indistinct soft-tissue boundaries and clinical rule-based delineation criteria that data-driven models capture only imprecisely. We formulate automated PA_rest segmentation as a clinically defined measurement task, translating an implicit clinical measurement into an explicit landmark specification and annotation protocol developed with a rehabilitation medicine specialist. Applying this protocol, we constructed, to our knowledge, the first dataset for this task: 2,255 single-center VFSS frames from 137 patients, with PA_rest contours and seven landmarks verified by a senior specialist. We then introduce GAG-Net, an automated rest-frame measurement pipeline combining deformable convolutions, for irregular pharyngeal boundaries, with a graph-based anatomical guidance module that models the geometric dependencies among landmarks prescribed by the delineation rules. On a patient-level held-out test set (237 frames, 67 patients), GAG-Net achieved the lowest area measurement error (mean absolute percentage error: 8.17% against specialist-verified references; patient-level ICC 0.97) and the highest Dice score (0.8862) among all evaluated methods, with 67.2% fewer parameters and 74% less training memory than the two-stage JOINED model. Integrating clinician-defined anatomical knowledge may enable automated PA_rest measurement from VFSS images alone, supporting quantitative assessment of sarcopenic dysphagia without supplementary imaging.

title: Emerging molecular mechanisms of immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.
desc: [International immunopharmacology] Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC) represents the predominant subtype of colorectal cancer and shows limited responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) monotherapy. This review summarizes the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying ICI resistance and discusses strategies to enhance immunotherapy sensitivity. Resistance in MSS CRC is mainly shaped by three interrelated barriers. First, low tumor immunogenicity, characterized by low tumor mutational burden, limited neoantigen generation, and impaired antigen presentation, weakens immune recognition. Second, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment enriched with tumor-associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory T cells, and cancer-associated fibroblasts restricts cytotoxic T-cell infiltration and function. Third, aberrant tumor-intrinsic signaling, metabolic and epigenetic alterations, and microbiota-mediated immune modulation further promote immune evasion. To overcome these barriers, combination strategies are being explored, particularly ICIs with anti-angiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), chemotherapy, radiotherapy, dual-checkpoint blockade, and therapies targeting myeloid cells, stromal components, or microbiota. Recent clinical evidence supports the potential of TKI-ICI combinations in selected patients. Future progress will depend on biomarker-guided patient selection integrating molecular subtyping, liquid biopsy, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence to identify responsive MSS CRC subsets and enable precision immunotherapy.

title: KMed-31B Technical Report
desc: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and diagnosis prediction have reference answers, whereas clinical inquiry has no single correct response and is judged with rubrics. We therefore divide medical training tasks into four categories by these two properties, train one specialist per category with a reward that its feedback supports, and integrate the specialists into a single student with Multi-teacher On-policy Delta Distillation (MOPD$^2$). For clinical inquiry, we build Synthetic Health Dialogue, a simulated corpus of consultations with lay users and clinicians whose patient cases span common clinical presentations in primary care. Relative to its base model, KMed-31B raises HealthBench Hard from 22.95 to 41.87 and HealthBench Professional from 37.92 to 50.20 in non-thinking mode, and from 23.80 to 51.48 and from 41.97 to 59.18 in thinking mode, while its scores on four multiple-choice medical benchmarks are maintained or slightly improved. KMed-31B has the highest unadjusted HealthBench Hard score among the compared models, including proprietary ones, and scores higher on HealthBench Professional than every open-weight model we compare, including models with more than ten times as many total parameters. Applied to another base model, Qwen3.8-27B, the same training recipe also raises both HealthBench scores. We describe the training recipe, data construction, and settings in detail so that institutions requiring on-premises deployment can develop medical models from open-weight foundations.

title: Real-Time Prediction of Cardiac Parameters Using Livestream Transthoracic Echocardiography Images: A Feasibility Study.
desc: [Ultrasound in medicine & biology] The aim of this study is to develop a workflow for acquiring and analyzing livestream echocardiography images from a GE HealthCare Vivid E95 system, a real-time artificial intelligence (AI)-based automatic left ventricle segmentation, and cardiac parameter prediction. The system provides automated echocardiography image analysis independent of electrocardiogram signals. A software pipeline was developed to acquire and analyze livestream echocardiography images from the ultrasound system. A UNet neural network model was trained using publicly available datasets (CAMUS, EchoNet-Dynamic) and an in-house dataset (Physical Activity and Fitness in Childhood Cancer Survivors). AI models were trained using these three datasets and three loss functions, with each model evaluated independently on all three test datasets. The model with the highest Dice score on the test datasets was selected and used to process livestream echocardiography images throughout the entire cardiac cycle. The resulting segmentation masks were used to compute the cardiac parameters. The offline-trained UNet models achieved an average Dice score of 0.9509. The livestream echocardiography image prediction showed average ejection fractions of 48%, 48% and 56%, corresponding to the Simpson's single-plane, area-length and Bullet methods, respectively. In contrast, EchoPAC (the GE HealthCare software tool to compute cardiac parameters) showed an average ejection fraction of 55% in nine volunteers with no known cardiac diseases. This study shows the feasibility of AI-assisted echocardiographic image analysis based on livestream echocardiography. However, the accuracy of the obtained cardiac parameters needs improvement to align with clinical standards.

title: Genome-to-Image Translation: Reconstructing Escherichia coli Morphology from Genomic Sequences
desc: Antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli is established in routine practice by culture-based susceptibility testing, which is slow relative to the clinical need for an early treatment decision. Resistance status also leaves a measurable trace in cell morphology, and whole-genome sequencing of clinical isolates is increasingly available, which raises the question of whether colony appearance can be predicted directly from an isolate's genome. We formulate this as a conditional image-generation problem. The assembled contigs of each isolate are encoded into a single 768-dimensional vector by a frozen genomic language model through a segment-contig-isolate aggregation hierarchy, and a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty synthesizes colony images from this embedding together with the applied antibiotic and the resistance label. We train on 167,356 single-cell images from 22 clinical blood isolates imaged under azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and a no-drug control, compare seven pretrained convolutional backbones inside the generator, and select ConvNeXt-Tiny on distributional image-quality metrics. The synthetic images are then assessed extrinsically: added to a reduced real training set, they improve per-antibiotic resistance classification, with a significant gain in resistant-class recall.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Natural Product Pharmacology: From Molecular Discovery to Precision Therapeutics.
desc: [Pharmacological research] The use of natural products as a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules for drug development has been well established; however, their multicomponent and multitarget nature, uncertain target causality, variable in vivo exposure, and heterogeneous responses to therapy make them challenging to characterize pharmacologically and translate into clinical practice. Systems pharmacology, together with artificial intelligence (AI), provides new approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, integration of multidimensional data, and development of precision therapeutics. Osteoarthritis (OA), a heterogeneous whole-joint disease characterized by inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic dysfunction, and tissue remodeling, serves as a representative model for evaluating such approaches. Network pharmacology can be used to organize relationships among natural product constituents, disease-related targets, and signaling pathways. AI can further assist with activity prediction, compound and target prioritization, multi-omics integration, and patient stratification. Studies combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, deep-learning-based affinity prediction, and experimental validation to narrow the list of potential candidate constituents and targets demonstrate the utility of computational methods in candidate prioritization. This article describes the transition of natural product pharmacology from empirical discovery and systems-based analysis to AI-enabled molecular discovery, mechanistic interpretation, pharmacokinetic assessment, and precision therapeutics. Although computational approaches may facilitate the identification and prioritization of biologically active constituents and targets, they remain limited by uncertainty regarding causality, inadequate in vivo exposure, model dependence, and insufficient clinical evidence. Future studies should focus on precise active-compound identification, direct target validation, systematic pharmacokinetic assessment, and high-quality clinical research to enhance the reliability and translational value of AI-enabled natural product pharmacology.

title: Decompose and Describe: Narrowing the Diagnosis-to-Report Gap in 3D CT Report Generation
desc: Automated 3D CT report generation could support radiology workflows, yet medical vision-language models (MedVLMs) often omit diagnostic findings from generated reports. We ask whether the diagnostic ability of these models carries over to free-form reporting. Across five MedVLMs, diagnostic VQA achieves higher macro-F1 than reports generated from the same CT studies and evaluated on the same disease categories. We call this task-dependent discrepancy the diagnosis-to-report gap. Conventional Report Adaptation improves reporting for most models but does not close the gap. To investigate and narrow it, we introduce DeCAD (Decompose CT Analysis and Describe), which progressively decomposes CT report generation at diagnostic, regional textual, and regional visual levels. The model identifies positive findings before writing a report, organizes diagnosis and description into regional tasks, and restricts each task to visual tokens from the corresponding region. Diagnostic and regional textual decomposition improve report-level diagnostic performance across the five MedVLMs, whereas regional visual decomposition provides limited additional gains. In a standard VLM without medical VQA pretraining, the first two levels remain effective; regional visual decomposition also provides further gains with a region-level contrastively pretrained encoder. Full DeCAD achieves state-of-the-art performance on CT-RATE and Merlin. Analyses show greater CT-token attention during diagnosis and higher recall of reference-positive findings in both the diagnostic output and final report than with Report Adaptation. These results show that explicitly organizing diagnosis improves diagnostic reporting and helps narrow the diagnosis-to-report gap.

title: Artificial Intelligence Series: Data Modalities and Clinical Applications in Rhinoplasty.
source: PubMed · Facial plastic surgery & aesthetic medicine
desc: [Facial plastic surgery & aesthetic medicine] Rhinoplasty requires individualized decisions that balance nasal appearance, airway function, structural support, and patient expectations. This narrative review examines artificial intelligence (AI) applications across the data modalities encountered in rhinoplasty care, emphasizing their potential roles in assessment, counseling, surgical planning, and outcome evaluation. Relevant modalities include clinical text, structured clinical data, facial photographs, anatomical imaging and three-dimensional surface geometry, and specialized measurements of surgical technique, nasal function, and visual perception. Clinical applications include patient counseling, organization of clinical records, risk and outcome prediction, quantitative nasal assessment, visualization of proposed changes, and postoperative evaluation. Multimodal and agentic systems may integrate these sources and tasks. Limitations include measurement errors, uncertain prediction of surgical outcomes, and limited evidence of improved clinical decisions or patient outcomes. Matching clinical questions to available data provides a practical framework for AI research and application in rhinoplasty. Standardized acquisition, secure linkage of longitudinal records, and independent validation are needed to support reproducible assessment and outcomes research. Surgeon oversight remains essential, with clinical value judged by functional and aesthetic outcomes and alignment with patient goals.

title: CT-Navigator: Towards Interpretable and Generalizable CT Understanding through Agentic Perception and Tool-Invocation
desc: Clinical computed tomography (CT) interpretation inherently requires progressive visual exploration, where radiologists navigate from whole scans to individual slices and regions of interest and interact with external tools when necessary. However, existing 3D medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) typically connect a specialized 3D visual encoder to a language model, without fully leveraging the native 2D visual and agentic capabilities of generalist MLLMs. Trained on large-scale one-hop CT instruction-following data, these models also have limited ability to perform iterative reasoning and explicitly ground their conclusions in visual evidence, limiting their support for traceable CT interpretation. To solve these problems, we propose \textbf{agentic perception} as an alternative paradigm inspired by radiologists' interpretation workflows. We introduce \textbf{CT-Navigator}, a framework that harnesses generalist MLLMs' 2D visual and agentic capabilities to progressively ground CT interpretation in explicit, traceable visual evidence through hierarchical visual exploration and radiology tool invocation. To build these capabilities, we curate 8,904 visual chain-of-thought (V-CoT) trajectories for cold-start agentic supervised fine-tuning. We then optimize the policy through reinforcement learning on 33,219 questions, with data selection and dynamic rollout sampling prioritizing informative learning signals. Finally, we introduce CTNavi-Bench, a 3D CT visual question answering benchmark comprising 7,000 questions spanning anatomical regions throughout the human body. CT-Navigator achieves 79.50\% accuracy on CTNavi-Bench, surpassing the strongest baseline by 17.59\%, and demonstrates strong generalization across three external CT benchmarks. The code, model, and benchmark will be released on \href{https://github.com/fyb99/ct_navigator}{GitHub}.

title: Artificial intelligence predictive medicine: geometric morphometrics in assisted scoliosis diagnosis.
source: PubMed · European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
desc: [European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society] Accurate scoliosis screening is essential for early intervention and to minimize unnecessary exposure to radiographic imaging. This study presents a landmark-based approach using Geometric Morphometric Methods combined with Elastic Net regression for the automated, non-invasive detection of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis from 3D torso surface scans. A retrospective cross-sectional study was performed on 168 individuals (135 with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis and 33 controls) using automatic landmark extraction on surface meshes from previous studies. After dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis, the resulting shape variables were used to train a logistic regression model with regularization. The main outcome measures were Area Under the Curve, sensitivity, specificity and balanced accuracy to estimate the performance metrics of the Artificial Intelligence screening model. The model showed high discriminative ability on an unseen test dataset (Area Under the Curve = 0.926; 95% CI: 0.816-1.000). When a classification threshold derived exclusively from the training set was applied to the test set, sensitivity was 100%, specificity was 14.3%, and balanced accuracy was 57.1%. In contrast to deep learning models, this approach offers an interpretable framework based on anatomical landmarks and does not require large datasets or extensive computational resources. The findings support further investigation of surface trunk morphology as a source of discriminative information for AIS detection. External validation in larger and more representative populations is required before clinical screening application.

title: Decoupling Perception from Generation for Agentic 3D CT Report Generation
desc: Chest CT reports repeatedly assess the same anatomical regions for findings and their attributes, such as whether a lung nodule is present and where it is located. These assessments suggest learning to answer visual questions directly, rather than coupling perception to open-ended text generation. Yet current CT report generation models largely follow generic vision-language modeling, which may miss subtle abnormalities when training data are limited. We therefore formulate report generation as a set of visual question-answering decisions coordinated by a large language model (LLM) agent. This decouples visual perception from reasoning and report writing: perception can be learned as a discriminative, non-generative task, while the LLM focuses on reasoning over patient context and posing relevant visual queries. We introduce Rad-VL-JEPA, which unifies report retrieval, finding recognition, and fine-grained attribute characterization through vision-language joint-embedding prediction. Building on this perception module, an agent trained with reinforcement learning (RL) acquires patient-specific visual evidence, while a separate editor incorporates the evidence into the final report, further separating evidence acquisition from report realization. Experiments show that Rad-VL-JEPA achieves strong performance on fine-grained CT understanding tasks with lower amortized per-query inference time than a generative VLM baseline trained with the same CT encoder and VQA data. The resulting reporting system outperforms strong VLM-based and agentic baselines.

title: Automated tool support for brain tumor diagnosis with explainability using MRI images.
desc: [Computational biology and chemistry] Precise and early detection of brain tumors is very important for successful clinical decision making. However the prevailing models didn't perform well on noisy images, also they didn't perform feature extraction to gather relevant tumor information. Most of the existing models produce good detection results with high complex architecture, increasing computational expensive. Moreover, these models have less interpretability and lacking accurate tumor detection, decreasing clinical decision making capability. To solve these issues, lightweight deep learning (DL) models is proposed in this research for accurate tumor segmentation and classification. This system include phase's namely pre-processing, segmentation, feature extraction, classification, model optimization and explainability. Experimental results are conducted on BraTS 2020 and BraTS 2018 datasets, proposed model produced accuracy of 99.75%, and 99.5% respectively.

title: Aegis: A Conversational Prototype for Lung Cancer Risk Information and Follow-up
desc: Collecting self-reported risk information and maintaining continuity between assessment, explanation, and follow-up are practical components of a lung cancer screening workflow. We present Aegis, a browser-based research prototype that combines a conversational questionnaire, rule-based risk categorization, downloadable reports, retrieval-augmented health information, and doctor-user communication. A session-oriented controller manages question progression and clarification, while a language model assists with answer validation. Structured responses are passed to a separate risk-analysis module, and reports are linked to user and session records through Firebase services. The project adopts a multi-agent design that separates information collection, validation, assessment, and report generation. Its documented verification scope comprises 45 functional test specifications covering account management, questionnaire interaction, reporting, doctor-side review, and consultation. The available evaluation describes workflow behavior qualitatively; it provides no per-case execution results, clinical cohort, predictive-performance measurements, or comparative experiments. We therefore present Aegis as an engineering prototype for organizing risk information and follow-up, with clinical validity and the benefits of its agent-based design remaining unestablished. The paper describes the implementation, distinguishes implemented workflows from incomplete extensions, and identifies the evidence required for reproducible and clinically meaningful evaluation.

title: Development and Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Driven Multigene Assay Decision-Support System for Personalized Management of T1 High-Grade Bladder Cancer.
desc: [MedComm] T1 high-grade bladder cancer presents a therapeutic dilemma, as current risk stratification fails to guide the choice between early cystectomy and bladder-preserving therapy. In our recent work, we defined a high-risk multiomic subtype driven by anoikis resistance and immune evasion and developed the T1HG-UCBguider framework for risk stratification; however, its reliance on multiomic sequencing limits clinical implementation. Here, we translate this framework into Guider, an artificial intelligence-driven reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) decision-aid designed for cost-conscious use in routine pathology workflows and integrating a 30-gene TaqMan assay with clinicopathological variables to predict progression and recurrence, with exploratory treatment-context modules for no instillation, Bacillus Calmette-Guérin, and intravesical chemotherapy. In a multicenter ambispective cohort of 1198 patients, Guider achieved > 10% higher absolute predictive performance than guideline-based risk groups and the published 12-gene progression score within this Chinese T1 high-grade cohort. Reclassification identified 82.5% of guideline-defined high-risk patients who progressed and 45.1% of very-high-risk nonprogressors who might be considered for bladder preservation. Guider could potentially support treatment de-escalation in 29.7% and escalation in 12.9% of patients. These findings establish a scalable translational framework bridging multiomic discovery and clinical decision support, warranting prospective interventional validation in geographically, ethnically, and demographically diverse populations.

title: CLASP: Deciding Structure and Claims Before Decoding for Whole-Slide Pathology Report Generation
desc: Whole-slide pathology report generation has advanced through stronger slide encoders, retrieved knowledge, and, recently, slide-level multimodal LLMs. However, these generators leave every report-level choice to the decoder: how long the report is, how it is organised, and which findings it states and where. On the standard PathText-BRCA benchmark, we find that these choices dominate n-gram overlap, as reports from the query's hospital selected without learning approach the state of the art, while decoders under-generate and fall back to the most frequent findings. We present CLASP, a decide-then-decode generator that makes these choices explicitly, once per slide. Before decoding, an Exemplar Structure Prior (ESP) takes the sentence plan and length from reports of image-similar cases, a Calibrated Claim Decision (CCD) selects the findings from calibrated slide posteriors, and a Claim-to-Sentence Placement (CSP) assigns each finding to a planned sentence. A Plan-Conditioned Decoder (PCD), refined by structure-anchored sequence training, then writes the report under these decisions. With 35M parameters, CLASP outperforms retrained report generators and slide-level LLMs of up to 7B parameters, matches the strongest published results, and generalises to lung cancer from unseen hospitals. Its decisions change what the reports state, not only their length, transfer to an LLM decoder, and can withhold what H&E cannot show: withholding receptor status leaves 23% fewer contradictions with clinical records than the same network without decisions.

title: Perioperative hemodynamic optimization.
source: PubMed · Current opinion in critical care
desc: [Current opinion in critical care] Perioperative hemodynamic optimization using goal-directed therapy (GDT) reduces complications and mortality in high-risk surgery. This review synthesizes advances over the last few years, focusing on dynamic physiological targets, predictive artificial intelligence, microcirculatory and endothelial protection, individualized arterial pressure targets, volume stewardship and novel nonadrenergic rescue vasopressors for postcardiopulmonary bypass vasoplegia, and extracorporeal blood purification for refractory vasoplegia in surgical sepsis. Clinical practice has shifted from rigid volumetric protocols toward individualized physiological stewardship and endothelial glycocalyx preservation, framed within the four-phase dynamic continuum (ROSE concept: Resuscitation, Optimization, Stabilization, and Evacuation). Machine-learning algorithms, such as the Hypotension Prediction Index, effectively preempt intraoperative hypotension. Point-of-care ultrasound protocols, notably the venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) score, prevent backward venous congestion. Concurrently, dynamic arterial elastance (Eadyn) distinguishes between vasodilation and preload deficit. In cardiothoracic surgery, postcardiopulmonary bypass vasoplegia mandates cautious fluid restriction and early multimodal nonadrenergic vasopressors, including methylene blue, hydroxocobalamin (vitamin B12), and synthetic angiotensin II, which effectively restore vascular tone and limit catecholamine toxicity. In surgical sepsis and refractory vasoplegic shock, blood purification therapies provide valuable hemodynamic rescue; the pioneer continuous hemodiafiltration with cytokine-adsorbing hemofilters (CAH-CHDF) and recent trial data with polymyxin B hemoperfusion (the TIGRIS trial) demonstrate significant vasopressor-sparing effects and restored vascular tone. Perioperative hemodynamic optimization has evolved into a multimodal, patient-tailored approach. Coupling dynamic fluid responsiveness with predictive monitoring, personalized blood pressure titration, nonadrenergic rescue for postbypass vasoplegic shock, organ venous congestion profiling, and extracorporeal humoral modulation provides comprehensive circulatory support while preventing fluid overload.

title: When AI Performance Is Not Enough: Statistical Guardrails for Clinical Development
desc: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are reshaping the operational and inferential landscape of clinical development, yet their adoption frequently outpaces the statistical scrutiny these methods demand. This commentary offers first-principles perspectives across four application domains: anomaly detection in clinical trial data, real-time monitoring and adaptive trial designs, biomarker-based enrichment, and virtual and digital twins. For each domain, we articulate the underlying inferential problem, the contribution of AI and ML relative to established statistical methods, and the risks that statisticians, data scientists, and clinical developers must actively manage. Across these domains, a unifying theme emerges: AI and ML methods may succeed locally while failing to satisfy the broader statistical assumptions required for valid clinical and regulatory decisions. These risks include false-positive signals, compromised Type I error control in adaptive designs, conflation of prognostic with predictive biomarkers, and causal claims not supported by data and assumptions. We argue that a clearly defined context of use, relevant statistical assumptions, and consequences of the intended decision should guide the evaluation. For treatment-effect questions, the ICH E9(R1) estimand framework provides a useful organizing principle. Responsible use of AI in clinical development requires not restraint, but rigor: the inferential discipline necessary to make these technologies reproducible, interpretable, and defensible in the service of patients.

title: Neuroscience-informed psychoeducation for epilepsy.
desc: [Progress in brain research] Epilepsy is among the most burdensome neurological disorders worldwide, with an impact that extends far beyond seizure frequency alone. Depression, anxiety, cognitive impairment, and internalized stigma affect a substantial proportion of individuals with epilepsy, yet these comorbidities remain systematically undertreated in routine neurological care. Conventional psychoeducation, largely centered on passive information delivery, has shown limited effectiveness in addressing the psychological and social complexities of living with epilepsy. Neuroscience-Informed Psychoeducation for Epilepsy (NIPE) offers a fundamentally different approach: one that translates the neuroscience of seizure generation, network dysfunction, and neuroplasticity into accessible frameworks, shifting patients from passive recipients of information to active, metacognitively engaged participants in their own care. This chapter presents NIPE as both a clinical framework and an integrative layer across the continuum of epilepsy management. Beginning with the neurobiological mechanisms underlying seizures and epileptogenesis, it highlights how the same neural networks implicated in ictal activity also contribute to the psychiatric and cognitive comorbidities that shape patients' daily experiences. It further examines how NIPE interfaces with evidence-based psychological interventions, pharmacologic education, neuromodulation, epilepsy surgery, and the management of refractory epilepsy, as well as the unique needs of women and other populations with distinct clinical considerations. In addition, the chapter explores the digital expansion of NIPE, including adaptive telehealth platforms, wearable biosensors, digital phenotyping, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence in tailoring psychoeducational delivery. Importantly, it addresses current limitations and ethical considerations with transparency, including the absence of standardized NIPE protocols and the relative scarcity of randomized controlled trials specifically within epilepsy populations. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking perspective on the infrastructure, research agenda, and cross-disciplinary collaboration required to embed NIPE into routine epileptology practice. NIPE is positioned not as an adjunct to epilepsy care, but as a unifying framework, a shared language that enables truly integrated, patient-centered care.

title: When Can an AI Agent Serve as a Model of Human Psychopathology?
desc: Language models and AI agents are increasingly described in psychiatric terms, such as anxious, depressed, addicted or helpless. A recent study even proposed language models as experimental systems for psychiatry and as a platform for piloting psychological treatments. We ask when an experiment on an AI agent can provide evidence about a specified human psychiatric process. A claim to such evidence has three parts. Something changed in the agent, and the agent's history caused the change. Nothing other than a process shared with people explains that change. The change matches one theory of the human process and not that theory's rivals. Psychiatry and its neighbouring fields have an evidence standard for each part, from the diagnostic manuals' rule for induced states, from clinical test scores and from animal models. We translate each standard into a criterion that a machine study can meet. For a language model the most critical alternative to a shared process is extrapolation from its training text, which already contains descriptions of how people respond to trauma and how they answer questionnaires. We show how to probe that alternative. Further, we audited forty-three published studies that apply psychiatric terms to a machine or induce a comparable state in one. Most compared the machine with an identical copy that had not gone through the history that induced the state. None excluded extrapolation from training text. Three tested a psychiatric theory against its rivals, and none of the three tests was conclusive. Until better evidence exists, a treatment pilot on a language model is best read as the model's forecast of patient response, and not as an experiment on a model organism. Evidence for a model organism will come from states induced by what happens to the machine, from experiments on its internal workings, and from tests on which rival theories disagree.

title: A multilingual mobile application for digital mental health support, emotional tracking, and therapist interaction.
desc: [Frontiers in digital health] Depression and other mental health challenges can affect daily functioning and well-being, while social stigma and limited access to culturally appropriate digital resources may discourage individuals from seeking support. This study presents REWAA, a bilingual mobile application designed to support emotional self-tracking, access to mental health resources, and interaction with mental health professionals in Arabic and English. REWAA was developed as an Android application with separate patient and therapist interfaces. Its features include mood self-tracking, an exploratory AI-based facial-analysis tool, the Bilingual Hybrid Mood Heuristic (BHMH) protocol, an AI-supported conversational tool, mental wellness resources, peer support groups, and therapist communication. The application was evaluated through a user survey involving 200 respondents to assess usability, perceived usefulness, emotional awareness, privacy, and user acceptance. Survey responses indicated generally positive perceptions of REWAA. Most respondents rated the graphical user interface as comfortable and easy to navigate (70%), while 60% reported that the REWAA bot helped them better understand their feelings and provided practical advice. In addition, 55% reported a significant improvement in emotional awareness, and 65% considered the application useful alongside professional therapy. Overall, the findings indicate positive user perceptions of the application's accessibility and integrated support features. REWAA demonstrates the potential of a bilingual digital platform to bring emotional self-tracking, supportive resources, and therapist interaction together in one application.
